chapter.title: The data
chapter.subtitle: Three years of public records
chapter.sub: Chapter three: the data. Let's see which records this study works with.
chapter.tts: Chapter three. The data. Let's see which records this study works with.

lines.sub: The data are the public records of Arbitrum One.
lines.tts: The data are the public records of Arbitrum One.

lines.sub: Let me spread three years of them out on this time axis.
lines.tts: Let me spread three years of them out on this time axis.

lines.sub: The observation window runs from 1 October 2023 to 30 June 2026: 33 months.
lines.tts: The observation window runs from the first of October twenty twenty-three to the thirtieth of June twenty twenty-six, thirty-three months.

lines.sub: The amber band on top is the approval records created each month.
lines.tts: The amber band on top is the approval records created each month.

lines.sub: The sky-blue band below is the transfer records.
lines.tts: The sky-blue band below is the transfer records.

lines.sub: Each band is scaled to its own height, so please compare only their shapes.
lines.tts: Each band is scaled to its own height, so please compare only their shapes.

lines.sub: Add the three months of the label window W1, and it is exactly three years.
lines.tts: Add the three months of the label window W one, and it is exactly three years.

card.title: Label window
card.body: A later stretch of time whose events are used to grade the scores

lines.sub: We tested twice.
lines.tts: We tested twice.

lines.sub: In W0, the scores were frozen on 31 March 2026, at the marker t₁.
lines.tts: In W zero, the scores were frozen on the thirty-first of March twenty twenty-six, at the marker t one.

lines.sub: Frozen means fixed on that day and not changed afterwards.
lines.tts: Frozen means fixed on that day and not changed afterwards.

lines.sub: They were then graded on what happened from April to June.
lines.tts: They were then graded on what happened from April to June.

lines.sub: In W1, the scores were frozen on 30 June, at T_obs, the end of the observation window.
lines.tts: In W one, the scores were frozen on the thirtieth of June, at T obs, the end of the observation window.

lines.sub: They were graded on what happened from July to September.
lines.tts: They were graded on what happened from July to September.

lines.sub: This study extracted those three months of records only after the grading rules were committed to a public repository.
lines.tts: This study extracted those three months of records only after the grading rules were committed to a public repository.

lines.sub: That commit was the registration: the rules were fixed in public, in advance.
lines.tts: That commit was the registration. The rules were fixed in public, in advance.

lines.sub: That is why there is a lock on it.
lines.tts: That is why there is a lock on it.

lines.sub: Last is the age ruler.
lines.tts: Last is the age ruler.

lines.sub: The time weight is measured backward from T_obs, that is, 30 June 2026.
lines.tts: The time weight is measured backward from T obs, that is, the thirtieth of June twenty twenty-six.

lines.sub: The oldest record is 1,004 days old.
lines.tts: The oldest record is one thousand and four days old.

lines.sub: This ruler comes back later, when I explain the time weight.
lines.tts: This ruler comes back later, when I explain the time weight.

lines.sub: Let me start with the volume of records.
lines.tts: Let me start with the volume of records.

lines.sub: Across the five tokens, I counted only the records that have a contract under study at one end.
lines.tts: Across the five tokens, I counted only the records that have a contract under study at one end.

lines.sub: I call these the cohort contracts. We will soon see how they were chosen.
lines.tts: I call these the cohort contracts. We will soon see how they were chosen.

lines.sub: The period is the 33-month observation window.
lines.tts: The period is the thirty-three-month observation window.

lines.sub: More than 220 million approval records: exactly 224,954,202.
lines.tts: More than two hundred twenty million approval records. Exactly two hundred twenty-four million, nine hundred fifty-four thousand, two hundred and two.

lines.sub: And more than 1.1 billion transfer records: exactly 1,149,168,538.
lines.tts: And more than one point one billion transfer records. Exactly one billion, one hundred forty-nine million, one hundred sixty-eight thousand, five hundred thirty-eight.

lines.sub: The line behind each number is the records piling up month by month.
lines.tts: The line behind each number is the records piling up month by month.

lines.sub: Below, one dot is 1 million records, so approvals make 225 dots and transfers 1,149.
lines.tts: Below, one dot is one million records, so approvals make two hundred twenty-five dots and transfers one thousand one hundred forty-nine.

lines.sub: Stacked again as bars, the same dots make the difference in length easy to see.
lines.tts: Stacked again as bars, the same dots make the difference in length easy to see.

lines.sub: There are about five times as many transfers as approvals.
lines.tts: There are about five times as many transfers as approvals.

lines.sub: Approvals happen much more rarely than transfers.
lines.tts: Approvals happen much more rarely than transfers.

lines.sub: For comparison, when all tokens were extracted, as first planned, there were about 390 million approval records and 1.5 billion transfer records.
lines.tts: For comparison, when all tokens were extracted, as first planned, there were about three hundred ninety million approval records and one point five billion transfer records.

lines.sub: These are the numbers of the registered analysis.
lines.tts: These are the numbers of the registered analysis.

lines.sub: The W1 records from July to September were extracted by this study separately, after the registration.
lines.tts: The W one records from July to September were extracted by this study separately, after the registration.

lines.sub: The cloud cost of all these queries was $34.80, within the budget of $50 set at the start.
lines.tts: The cloud cost of all these queries was thirty-four dollars and eighty cents, within the budget of fifty dollars set at the start.

lines.sub: Each token has its own unit and its own value, so amounts cannot simply be added together.
lines.tts: Each token has its own unit and its own value, so amounts cannot simply be added together.

lines.sub: That is why the revised analysis, the later version that followed the registered one, converted every amount to US dollars.
lines.tts: That is why the revised analysis, the later version that followed the registered one, converted every amount to US dollars.

lines.sub: The prices are DefiLlama daily closes, that is, the last price of each day.
lines.tts: The prices are DeFi Llama daily closes, that is, the last price of each day.

lines.sub: Five tokens remain: WETH, USDC, USDT0, ARB and WBTC.
lines.tts: Five tokens remain. Wrapped ether, U S D C, U S D T zero, A R B, and wrapped bitcoin.

lines.sub: Chainlink publishes price feeds on the chain.
lines.tts: Chainlink publishes price feeds on the chain.

lines.sub: Start with the tokens whose Chainlink feed is rated low or medium risk and that have a daily price. There are 46.
lines.tts: Start with the tokens whose Chainlink feed is rated low or medium risk, and that have a daily price. There are forty-six.

lines.sub: These five have the most records among them.
lines.tts: These five have the most records among them.

lines.sub: All five are priced by feeds rated low risk.
lines.tts: All five are priced by feeds rated low risk.

lines.sub: The vertical axis is a log scale, so everything from 0.1 dollars to 100,000 dollars fits in one picture.
lines.tts: The vertical axis is a log scale, so everything from zero point one dollars to one hundred thousand dollars fits in one picture.

card.title: Log scale
card.body: An axis where each step up means ten times more

lines.sub: WETH and WBTC swing up and down a lot.
lines.tts: Wrapped ether and wrapped bitcoin swing up and down a lot.

lines.sub: USDC and USDT0, on the other hand, stay almost fixed at one dollar.
lines.tts: U S D C and U S D T zero, on the other hand, stay almost fixed at one dollar.

lines.sub: They are stablecoins, made to track the dollar.
lines.tts: They are stablecoins, made to track the dollar.

lines.sub: So for a token like WETH, one coin can be worth a different number of dollars from day to day.
lines.tts: So for a token like wrapped ether, one coin can be worth a different number of dollars from day to day.

lines.sub: A transfer is converted at the price of the day it happened.
lines.tts: A transfer is converted at the price of the day it happened.

lines.sub: An allowance is converted at the price of the anchor day, the day the scores are frozen.
lines.tts: An allowance is converted at the price of the anchor day, the day the scores are frozen.

lines.sub: Those are t₁, 31 March, and T_obs, 30 June. The white dots mark those prices.
lines.tts: Those are t one, the thirty-first of March, and T obs, the thirtieth of June. The white dots mark those prices.

lines.sub: Why? An allowance is a promise that is still alive on that day.
lines.tts: Why? An allowance is a promise that is still alive on that day.

lines.sub: The units must match too.
lines.tts: The units must match too.

lines.sub: One USDC is a million base units, its smallest pieces. That is six zeros.
lines.tts: One U S D C is a million base units, its smallest pieces. That is six zeros.

lines.sub: One WETH has 18 zeros: 12 more than USDC.
lines.tts: One wrapped ether has eighteen zeros, twelve more than U S D C.

lines.sub: So we multiply the number of base units, v, by 10^−q, to get the number of tokens.
lines.tts: So we multiply the number of base units, v, by ten to the power minus q, to get the number of tokens.

lines.sub: Here q is the number of decimal places: 6 for USDC, 18 for WETH.
lines.tts: Here q is the number of decimal places, six for U S D C, eighteen for wrapped ether.

lines.sub: Then we multiply by that day's price, p, to get dollars.
lines.tts: Then we multiply by that day's price, p, to get dollars.

lines.sub: We will see this formula again with the value weight.
lines.tts: We will see this formula again with the value weight.

lines.sub: I also checked whether these prices can be trusted.
lines.tts: I also checked whether these prices can be trusted.

lines.sub: I compared them with the Chainlink prices on the chain, on 38 days for each token.
lines.tts: I compared them with the Chainlink prices on the chain, on thirty-eight days for each token.

lines.sub: Per token, the median difference was 0.01 to 0.08 percent. The median is the middle value.
lines.tts: Per token, the median difference was zero point zero one to zero point zero eight percent. The median is the middle value.

lines.sub: And the largest difference was 0.72 percent.
lines.tts: And the largest difference was zero point seven two percent.
